ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners and any limited partner controlling or benefiting from 25% or more of partnership interests against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and applicable domestic enforcement lists; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) must follow FINTRAC and OSFI guidance on source of wealth, source of funds, and relationship nature; negative news searches and corroborating commercial documentation must be retained for five years after termination of the business relationship as required by the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filing language is English or French; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet form; the statutory ending must include the words 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'; names must be distinctive from existing Ontario business names and not confuse the public as to jurisdiction, government sponsorship, or regulated professional status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, submit a written administrative reconsideration through the Ontario Business Registry portal within 30 days of rejection, attaching the original NUANS report, a memorandum explaining how the proposed name is distinguishable, and any consent letters from prior users; if the Registry still refuses, appeal to the Director under the applicable Ontario business statutes for final internal administrative review; legal counsel should prepare a supplementary affidavit of distinctiveness and corporate name search package before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a low-risk localization agency only if the virtual office includes a physical street address in Ontario, a named agent available during normal business hours, official mail handling, and a valid service-of-process location; a mail-only virtual address without physical Ontario presence is not sufficient for a registered limited partnership office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% to 10% annual probability of unannounced inspection or correspondence-based verification, driven by CRA tax-review triggers, FINTRAC AML anomaly alerts, or third-party complaints; no routine inspection mandate exists for translation and localization services.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, ss. 2 (formation), 3 (declaration), 8 (registration and amendment), 9 (records), 12 (liability of limited partner); Partnership Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.5 (supplementary rules); Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39 (annual returns); General Regulation, R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 748 (forms and fees)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPSB), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Province of Ontario
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 3 – Declaration of Limited Partnership filed under section 3 of the Limited Partnerships Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; limited partners may contribute capital in cash, property, or services per the Limited Partnership Agreement; no escrow account or capital deposit certificate required by the Registrar; capital contributions are set contractually and reflected in the agreement only
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby approves the filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership with ServiceOntario for the formation of the Ontario Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Limited Partnership Agreement annexed hereto is adopted in full and the subscriptions of the initial Limited Partners are accepted; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership shall be located at the address set forth in the Declaration and shall be the initial address for service; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed designated representative with authority to execute ancillary filings, open banking accounts, and administer daily operations; FURTHER RESOLVED, that all actions taken by officers within the scope of their delegated authority are ratified and indemnified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Clearance via NUANS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario (Companies and Personal Property Security Branch) through an authorized NUANS service provider; online portal: ServiceOntario e-Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request for the proposed limited partnership name, ensuring the name is distinctive and does not conflict with existing corporate, LP, or trademark registrations in Ontario. Receive the NUANS report and select the primary and alternate names. If the name includes 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP', the French equivalents ('Société en commandite' / 'SEC') may also be used for bilingual branding.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS request form
Proposed name (primary and two alternates)
NUANS search fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried for resemblance, file a written submission with the Director explaining the distinguishing elements, or select an alternate cleared name and re-file the NUANS report; consent letters from prior right holders may cure conflicts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPSB); online via ServiceOntario e-Filing or in person at a ServiceOntario centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 3 – Declaration of Limited Partnership, signed by each general partner (or authorized attorney-in-fact). Declare the partnership name, general nature of business (professional multilingual translation and media dubbing / localization agency), registered office address in Ontario (a physical, not post-office box, address), full names and addresses of all general partners, and term (if limited, otherwise perpetual). File with the statutory fee of CAD $60 plus applicable service charges; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form 3 – Declaration of Limited Partnership (executed)
NUANS name search report
Filing fee payment (CAD $60 via credit card or ServiceOntario account)
Written authorization/POA if a general partner signs through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried for deficiencies, the Registrar will issue a notice of default; correct and re-submit the Declaration within 30 days or request an extension in writing; amend the Declaration under section 8 and file Form 4 (Statement of Change) for any post-filing changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Federal Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; telephone 1-800-959-5525
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Limited Partnership from ServiceOntario, register the Ontario LP with the CRA to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN). Open a GST/HST account (required where worldwide taxable revenues exceed CAD $30,000), a payroll (RP) account if employees will be hired, and an import/export (RM) account if cross-border media delivery applies. The LP files its own T5013 Partnership Information Return annually; each limited partner reports allocated income separately.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Limited Partnership Agreement (for tax allocation schedules)
General partner's name, address, and BN/SIN
Banking details for CRA direct deposit (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond via My Business Account within 30 days; request retroactive correction if the BN is cross-referenced incorrectly; if a penalty is assessed for late registration, apply for taxpayer relief under the Income Tax Act subsection 220(3.1).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Tax Registration and Employer Health Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Finance – Ontario Business Registry (OBR) / provincial tax online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Ontario LP with the Ministry of Finance for any applicable provincial tax obligations. Employer Health Tax (EHT) registration is mandatory only if total Ontario payroll exceeds CAD $1,000,000 annually; a voluntary EHT registration is available. If the LP does not exceed the threshold, no EHT account is required, but the exemption must be documented. The LP must also file the annual return under the Corporations Information Act (via ServiceOntario).
required_dossiers: CRA Business Number and GST/HST account confirmation
Payroll estimate and headcount in Ontario
Evidence of Ontario payroll threshold status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry queries EHT status, submit payroll records proving the threshold is not met; if an assessment is issued, file a Notice of Objection within 180 days under the Employer Health Tax Act; update the Ontario Business Registry within 15 days of any governance change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning and Local Business Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal authority (e.g., City of Toronto – Municipal Licensing & Standards; zoning division and building department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the registered office / studio premises are zoned to permit a professional office and media production/dubbing studio (typically 'Office', 'Business & Professional' or 'Creative Studio' zoning classes). Apply for a municipal business license or an occupancy permit if required by the applicable municipal by-law; obtain a sign permit for exterior signage. For a localization agency operating remotely, a home-based business permit may suffice.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of property ownership
Zoning certificate / land use conformity letter
Municipal business license application (if applicable)
Sign permit application and design drawings (if signage is installed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning is non-conforming, apply to the Committee of Adjustment for a minor variance under section 45 of the Planning Act; if the business license is refused, appeal to the Licensing Tribunal or Municipal Standards Appeal Board within the statutory appeal window; otherwise relocate the registered office to compliant premises and amend the Declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Annual Filings and Continuity Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario (Corporations Information Act annual return) and Canada Revenue Agency (T5013 Partnership Information Return)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual return for the limited partnership with ServiceOntario each calendar year, no later than the anniversary of registration; file the T5013 and T5013SUM with the CRA on or before March 31 following each fiscal year end; issue T5013 slips/statements to each partner by March 31; maintain records of general and limited partners, capital contributions, and distributions as required by section 9 of the Limited Partnerships Act.
required_dossiers: Annual return filing (online via ServiceOntario)
T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013SUM
Partner capital account statements and fiscal year-end financial statements
Updated register of partners and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a late annual return triggers a notice of dissolution or administrative strike-off, file the overdue return and pay the CAD $210 reinstatement fee; for CRA late-filing penalties, submit a Voluntary Disclosures Program application (if eligible) or request penalty relief due to reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None – no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over professional translation and media dubbing services in Ontario; municipal zoning and building departments remain the only local authorities for physical premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no provincial operating license or sectoral permit is required for translation/localization services under Ontario law; a municipal occupancy permit and any applicable home-based business license satisfy physical site requirements

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP); local Conservation Authority for watercourse setbacks adjacent to studio premises
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based professional services fall outside the mandatory EIA categories of Ontario Regulation 133/07 (Environmental Assessment Act); no Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) is required absent industrial wastewater discharge, hazardous emissions, or waste generation above threshold quantities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If dubbing studio operates HVAC, acoustic insulation, or minor equipment: applicable limits under O. Reg. 419/05 (air emissions) and O. Reg. 347 (waste management); no industrial effluent is generated — sanitary discharges must comply with municipal sewer by-laws under the Ontario Water Resources Act; hazardous audio equipment batteries and electronic waste must be disposed through an approved hazardous waste carrier; noise attenuation for studio operations must satisfy local municipal noise by-laws (e.g., Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 591).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) – fire safety plan approval, smoke alarms, fire extinguishers, and annual inspection by the local fire marshal for commercial premises; Ontario Building Code Act – final inspection and occupancy certificate for studio fit-out (acoustic insulation, electrical upgrades); Occupational Health and Safety Act – workplace hazard assessment, ergonomic workstation compliance, and WHMIS training for cleaning chemicals; Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) – customer service and integrated accessibility standards (employment and information/communications) applicable once the workplace is operational.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online portal; Ontario Ministry of Finance for provincial aspects (HST is administered federally by CRA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership must obtain a Canadian Business Number (BN) and, if taxable supplies exceed the threshold, a separate GST/HST account. Apply through CRA Form RC1, online Business Registration, or by completing the non-resident registration form RC447. Ontario-specific province registration may be required only for provincial levies such as Employer Health Tax if the partnership has Ontario payroll; no separate Ontario corporate or partnership number is required for GST/HST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election. A limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes; each partner is taxed on their allocated share. For GST/HST, the partnership itself is a separate 'person' and a mandatory registrant once taxable supplies exceed the threshold. No hybrid mismatch election is available domestically; anti-hybrid rules apply under the Income Tax Act (Part VI.1) to conflicting entity classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made by the partnership; for non-residents, only supplies treated as made in Ontario/Canada are counted toward this threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance regime exists for GST/HST in Canada. CRA accepts electronic invoices and documents in standard formats; no digital stamping or API clearance is required. The pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework is optional and still voluntary as of the effective date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, when proof of export is retained. Services supplied to a non-resident person qualify for zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, Section 23 provided the non-resident is not a GST/HST registrant and the service is performed in whole or in part in Canada but is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property located in Canada. Localization, translation, and media dubbing services rendered to overseas clients will typically qualify as zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canadian Automated Export Declaration or B13A)
Bill of Lading or equivalent commercial shipping document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/Wise/Payoneer payment confirmation evidencing foreign-currency receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess the partnership to apply HST on the full invoice amount where export documentation is missing or insufficient. A knowingly false zero-rating claim is subject to gross-negligence penalties of up to 50% of the tax sought to be avoided, daily interest on the outstanding amount, and, in aggravated cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion. Retroactive cancellation of zero-rating triggers recapture of associated input tax credits previously claimed on expenses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) supervises AML/KYC; no dedicated foreign exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility under IMF Article VIII for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no prior approval requirement for foreign currency conversions, and no restriction on profit or capital distributions from a Canadian limited partnership to non-resident limited partners. Remittances to non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (typically 25% without treaty relief, reduced under Canada-U.S./Canada-U.K. tax treaties), but this is a tax matter, not a foreign exchange barrier. Since the LP is export-oriented and invoice-based, CAD/USD and CAD/EUR liquidity is fully fungible through bank swap desks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements. No timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export receipts to Canada within a certain period. Export receivables may be retained in foreign currency accounts (USD/EUR) at a Canadian chartered bank or held at a foreign bank subsidiary, subject to normal factual reporting under Canada's foreign income verification rules (Form T1135 if aggregate foreign property exceeds C$100,000).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for Wise B2B (Wise Edge Technologies Canada Inc.) and Payoneer as supplementary settlement rails, but LOW as primary banking substitutes. Canadian chartered banks remain mandatory for CAD clearing, CDIC-insured deposits, and irrevocable LC issuance. Under the Bank Act, Wise and Payoneer are money service businesses (MSBs) requiring FINTRAC registration; they do not hold banking licenses, cannot take demand deposits in the legal sense, and cannot provide credit. They are legally viable for cross-border vendor payments and small receipts, but must be linked to a Tier 1 corporate bank account for capital escrow and high-value trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in Ontario is strongly preferred and de facto standard for opening a Limited Partnership bank account at Tier 1 banks. At least one general partner (GP) or authorized signatory with 25% or more control over the LP must attend a new-to-bank verification interview in person at an Ontario branch, or complete a video call if the bank's discretionary remote-onboarding process is approved for a low-risk professional localization agency. Remote opening is permitted by OSFI guidance on a risk-based approach, but for a newly formed foreign-owned LP, Canadian banks typically require an in-branch meeting to evidence management substance. A Canadian-resident GP or registered Ontario agent is recommended to streamline the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership and control confusion: foreign corporate general partner with opaque upstream shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services Clearance/Certificate of Limited Partnership status; complete LP agreement; organizational chart of the general partner chain to ultimate natural persons; certificate of good standing from corporate registry of foreign GP; personal identification and proof of address for each individual holding 10% or greater; statutory declaration of source of funds for capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual purpose code or income pattern for a localization agency (e.g., large inbound wire labeled 'consulting' rather than 'production services')
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed localization service contracts (translation, dubbing, subtitling) with named counterparties; sample invoices and purchase orders; detailed board/general partner resolution describing the LP's treasury operations; invoices showing the AI/translation software licensing costs and media royalties to clarify the business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Involvement of a jurisdiction listed as FATF high-risk or non-cooperative (e.g., sanctions-sensitive counterparty)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions screening report (via World-Check or bank's FIS filter) clearing all ultimate beneficial owners; independent legal opinion on OFAC/OSFI sanctions and trade control exposure; practical explanation for the jurisdictional counterparty link; confirmation of no Canadian Economic Sanctions Act (SCAEMA) or United Nations Act violations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner receiving distributions without clear business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The Limited Partnership Agreement with waterfall provisions; section showing tax allocation and distribution mechanics; letter from Canadian counsel confirming non-resident LPs are passive investors and not involved in management; Form T2 or partnership information return (T5013) history if available; source-of-wealth statement for the LP's capital contributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: send via SWIFT MT103 from foreign parent/holding entity to the Ontario LP's CAD/USD pooled account at a Tier 1 chartered bank. Use purpose code FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) for paid-in capital, or 'GIN'/'BOND' if the injection is structured as a partnership contribution; in practice Canadian banks require a plain-English description such as 'LP capital contribution' to avoid FINTRAP misclassification. All cross-border electronic fund transfers (ETRs) of C$10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC within 24 hours per the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Banks verify the authenticity through the bank's SWIFT Reference, the sender's KYC profile at the instructing bank, and the LP's own source-of-funds statement. Confirm GFIP (Global Foreign Interbank Payment) details with correspondent bank to ensure the final beneficiary is the Ontario LP with its legal entity identifier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) settled by the issuing Canadian bank through SWIFT GPI, delivering same-day/1-day settlement to counterparties in EU, US, and Asia. Use separate 'TSU' or 'TRA' purpose codes for royalty/license fees; use 'TRD' for translation subcontractor payments. For high-value procurement of dubbing studios, subtitling platforms, or master license deals, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) denominated in USD/EUR, payable at sight, with negotiation of compliant documents. For regular payroll-like disbursements to linguists and invigilators, maintain pooled multi-currency accounts (USD/EUR/CAD) at RBC or BMO to avoid forced conversion and reduce FX spread. For low-value recurring streaming royalties, use Wise B2B and Payoneer settlement corridors; monitor their FINTRAC registration and CIPF uninsured status.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable commercial forward contracts (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) with standard ISDA or Canadian Master Agreement collateral terms
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for less liquid or restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, KRW, INR) where local convertibility is unavailable to a Canadian entity

Cross-currency swap agreements (fixed/floating or floating/floating) executed under ISDA with a Canadian Schedule, to simultaneously hedge notional and interest exposures emerging from multi-currency vendor contracts
Deep in-the-money Canadian FX options (collar or parity) used as a hedge when the LP's localization contracts generate strong accounting forecast against a deterministic FX exposure

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (9% federal rate on first $500,000 active business income) not applicable to LPs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T1 Personal Tax Return (individual partners) or T2 Corporate Tax Return (corporate partners); no separate entity-level return for LP
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: April 30 following taxation year for individuals; June 15 for businesses

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distributive share of partnership income or loss from the Limited Partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source income share; non-residents file T1 and may require NR4 reporting

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing $50 per day to max $2,000; failure to remit tax $5% per month on unpaid amount

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A - Distributions from LP not subject to withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners report share directly on personal return; no TRC or dividend relief required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties 0% under most treaties; interest 25% statutory rate, reduced to 10-15% under applicable tax treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 250,000 for related-party transactions triggering TP documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not applicable; Canada applies GAAR, transfer pricing rules and CFC provisions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting distributive share from personal tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion charges, fines up to $100,000, imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners personally liable for tax obligations and partnership debts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using LP for tax avoidance without substantive business activities
